certification.name: PyTorch Core: Practical ML & Neural Networks

concepts.name: `requires_grad`
concepts.description: `requires_grad=True` tells autograd to track operations needed to compute gradients with respect to that tensor in normal grad mode.

concepts.name: `loss.backward()`
concepts.description: `loss.backward()` computes gradients through the recorded graph and accumulates them into `.grad` fields of relevant leaf tensors.

concepts.name: Gradient accumulation
concepts.description: PyTorch accumulates parameter gradients by default, so each backward pass adds to existing `.grad` values.

concepts.name: `detach()`
concepts.description: `tensor.detach()` returns a tensor detached from the current autograd graph.

concepts.name: Clearing gradients
concepts.description: `optimizer.zero_grad()` clears or resets gradients associated with parameters managed by the optimizer.

concepts.name: `optimizer.step()`
concepts.description: `optimizer.step()` updates parameters using the gradients currently stored for the optimizer-managed parameters.

concepts.name: `loss.item()`
concepts.description: `loss.item()` converts a one-element tensor such as a scalar loss into a standard Python number.

concepts.name: `model.train()` and `model.eval()`
concepts.description: `model.train()` enables training behavior for mode-sensitive modules, while `model.eval()` switches them to evaluation behavior.

concepts.name: `torch.no_grad()`
concepts.description: `torch.no_grad()` disables recording operations for reverse-mode gradient calculation inside its context.

concepts.name: `torch.inference_mode()`
concepts.description: `torch.inference_mode()` disables autograd recording and removes additional autograd-related overhead for computations that will not later participate in grad-mode graphs.

concepts.name: Freezing parameters
concepts.description: Setting a parameter or module to `requires_grad_(False)` excludes those parameters from gradient computation in normal grad mode.

concepts.name: Gradient clipping
concepts.description: `torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_` clips the total norm of parameter gradients in place to a specified maximum norm.
